evidence_excerpts: Table 1 clearly shows that the upper bounds on the number of layers that result from compiling the layers of remote CNOTs are widely respected and hold for all the considered examples.
Fig. 15(c) also shows that choosing the data-qubit-swapping-based strategy against the entanglement-swapping-based strategy is generally the best choice.

text: Experimental validation on medium-size quantum circuits respected the analytical bounds, and the data-qubit-swapping strategy generally required fewer link-generation layers and lower circuit depth than entanglement swapping alone.
